items.prompt: Three spoons stand in hot soup. Which handle gets hot fastest?

figure.alt: A metal spoon, a wooden spoon and a plastic spoon standing in a bowl of hot soup.

options.why: Wood is a thermal insulator. Heat moves through it slowly.
Plastic is a thermal insulator. Heat moves through it slowly.

options.text: They all heat up at the same speed.
options.why: Different materials let heat through at different speeds.

hints: Heat travels up the spoon from the soup.
Some materials let heat through quickly.
Which material are cooking pans made of?
items.explanation: Metal is a good thermal conductor, so heat travels up the metal spoon quickly. Wood and plastic are thermal insulators.

items.prompt: Sort the materials. Do they conduct electricity?
hints: Most metals conduct electricity.
Plastic, rubber and wood do not.
Ask of each one: is it a metal?
items.explanation: Copper, steel and aluminium are metals, and metals conduct electricity. Plastic, rubber, wood, glass and paper are electrical insulators.

items.prompt: Why are electric wires covered in plastic?

options.why: Plastic does not carry electricity at all.
Plastic is an insulator, not a conductor.
Plastic is not magnetic.

options.text: Plastic is an electrical insulator, so it keeps us safe.

hints: The metal inside the wire carries electricity.
The covering stops electricity reaching your hand.
Is plastic a conductor or an insulator?
items.explanation: The metal inside carries the electricity. The plastic covering is an electrical insulator, so it stops electricity reaching us.

items.prompt: Many cooking pots have plastic or wooden handles. Why?

options.text: Plastic and wood are thermal insulators, so the handle stays cool.
They make the pot heat up faster.
options.why: The handle does not touch the flame. It is there for holding.

options.text: Plastic and wood are good thermal conductors.
options.why: They are poor conductors of heat. That is why they are used.
Weight is not the reason. Keeping hands safe is.

hints: The pot itself gets very hot.
You need to hold the handle safely.
Which materials let heat through slowly?
items.explanation: Plastic and wood are thermal insulators, so heat moves through them slowly. The handle stays cool enough to hold.

items.prompt: A metal bench and a wooden bench stand in the same shade. The metal one feels colder to touch. Why?

options.text: The metal bench is at a lower temperature.
options.why: Both benches are in the same shade at the same temperature.

options.text: Metal conducts heat away from your hand faster.

options.why: Wood does not make heat.
The metal bench is dry.

hints: Both benches are in the same place.
Your hand is warmer than both benches.
Which material takes heat from your hand faster?
items.explanation: Both benches are at the same temperature. Metal is a good thermal conductor, so it carries heat away from your hand quickly and feels colder.

items.prompt: Ice cubes were wrapped in different materials. Which material is the best thermal insulator?

head: Wrapping
Time to melt (minutes)
figure.alt: Table of melting times: no wrapping 20 minutes, foil 25 minutes, newspaper 40 minutes, wool 60 minutes.

options.why: Foil kept the ice only 5 minutes longer than no wrapping.
Newspaper helped, but another material kept the ice longer.
With no wrapping, the ice melted fastest.

hints: A good insulator slows heat getting to the ice.
So the best insulator gives the longest time.
Find the biggest number.
items.explanation: The ice wrapped in wool took 60 minutes to melt, the longest time. Wool slowed heat reaching the ice the most.

items.prompt: Choose 2 good thermal insulators.

options.why: Copper is a metal and a good conductor of heat.
Steel is a metal and conducts heat well.
Aluminium is a metal and conducts heat well.

hints: Thermal insulators let heat through slowly.
Metals are good conductors of heat.
Cross out the metals.
items.explanation: Wool and plastic foam trap air and let heat through slowly. They are good thermal insulators.

items.prompt: A thick wool jumper keeps you warm. How does it do this?

options.why: Wool does not make heat. Your body makes it.
A jumper keeps cold air out, not in.
Wool is a thermal insulator.

options.text: It traps air and slows down heat leaving your body.

hints: Your body makes heat all the time.
Something must slow down the heat escaping.
What is trapped between the woolly fibres?
items.explanation: Your body makes heat. Wool traps air between its fibres, and this slows down the heat escaping from your body.

items.prompt: Pencil lead is made of graphite. In a circuit, it makes a bulb glow dimly. What does this show?

options.text: Graphite conducts electricity, even though it is not a metal.

options.why: Graphite is a form of carbon. It is not a metal.
The bulb glows, so it works.
The wood around the lead is an insulator. The graphite conducts.

hints: The bulb glows, so electricity is flowing.
The electricity flows through the lead.
Is graphite a metal?
items.explanation: Graphite conducts electricity, even though it is not a metal. Graphite is a weak conductor, so the bulb glows dimly.

items.prompt: Bayu puts objects in the gap of this circuit. Which one makes the bulb light?

figure.alt: A circuit with a battery, a bulb and a gap where an object can be placed.

options.why: Plastic is an electrical insulator.
Rubber is an electrical insulator.
Paper is an electrical insulator.

hints: The object must let electricity through.
Electrical conductors are usually metals.
Which object is made of metal?
items.explanation: Steel is a metal, so it conducts electricity. The paperclip closes the gap and the bulb lights.

items.prompt: Ice cream is carried home in a box made of plastic foam. Why?

options.text: The foam makes the ice cream colder.
options.why: Foam does not make cold. It slows heat getting in.

options.text: The foam is a good thermal conductor.
options.why: Foam is a thermal insulator.

options.text: The foam is a thermal insulator, so the ice cream melts slowly.
The foam keeps the ice cream dry.
options.why: Ice cream is in its own tub. The foam is there to slow heat.

hints: Heat from the warm air can melt ice cream.
The box must slow down the heat getting in.
Is foam a conductor or an insulator of heat?
items.explanation: Plastic foam is a thermal insulator. It slows heat moving from the warm air to the ice cream, so it melts slowly.

items.prompt: A saucepan has a metal base and a plastic handle. Explain why. Use the words conductor and insulator.

criteria.label: Says the metal base is a thermal conductor
Says heat moves quickly through the base to the food

items.model: The base is metal because metal is a good thermal conductor, so heat moves quickly to cook the food. The handle is plastic because plastic is a thermal insulator, so it stays cool and safe to hold.
hints: Write one sentence about the base and one about the handle.
Say where you want heat to go, and where you do not.
items.explanation: The metal base is a thermal conductor, so heat moves quickly to the food. The plastic handle is a thermal insulator, so it stays cool to hold.
